title: Frozen Nematode Sample Preparation for Sequencing
author: Manuela Kieninger

steps.title: Seed plates with worms
steps.instruction: Place an equal number of adult females or hermaphrodites containing embryos on 9 cm NGM plates seeded with food bacteria; typically 20 worms per plate and prepare about 20 plates.

steps.title: Pre‑chill centrifuge
steps.instruction: Set a centrifuge that fits 50 ml and 15 ml tubes to 4 °C before use.

steps.title: Incubate plates at growth temperature
steps.instruction: Seal the plates with Parafilm, put them in a box and incubate at the species‑specific growing temperature until the bacterial lawn is gone or the plate is full of worms (do not let worms starve).

steps.title: Harvest worms with cold M9
steps.instruction: Add a small volume of fridge‑chilled M9 to each plate, gently swirl to release the worms, and pour the suspension into a 50 ml Falcon tube kept on ice; repeat across plates to avoid a large volume.

steps.title: First wash and pellet
steps.instruction: Fill the Falcon tube up to 40 ml with additional cold M9, invert several times, then spin at 2500 rcf for 8 min at 4 °C; carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Second wash with M9/Tween
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in chilled M9 containing 0.01 % Tween to a final volume of 14 ml and spin 2 min at 800 rcf (4 °C). Repeat this wash until the supernatant is clear (typically 2–3 washes).

steps.title: Final PBS wash
steps.instruction: Fill the tube to 14 ml with PBS, spin 2 min at 800 rcf; you now have clean worms ready for freezing.

steps.title: Adjust pellet volume
steps.instruction: Keep tubes on ice; if the pellet exceeds 2 ml, divide into multiple 15 ml tubes and top each up to 5 ml with cold M9/Tween.

steps.title: High‑speed spin for worm float
steps.instruction: Spin tubes 5 min at 3500 rcf at 4 °C; clean worms float to the top while bacteria and debris settle.

steps.title: Collect floating worms
steps.instruction: Using a transfer pipet washed in M9/Tween, aspirate the floating worms and transfer them to a new 15 ml Falcon tube.

substeps.instruction: Wash the transfer pipet with M9/Tween before use to prevent worm adhesion.

steps.title: Wash worms twice with M9/Tween
steps.instruction: Fill the tube with M9/Tween to 14 ml, spin 2 min at 800 rcf in a cold centrifuge (4 °C); repeat the wash once more.

steps.title: Aliquot worms into low‑bind tubes
steps.instruction: Add ~70–80 µl of worm suspension to 1.5 ml LoBind (or pestle) tubes, placing the worms at the bottom; use a low‑bind 200 µl tip pre‑wetted with M9/Tween.

steps.title: Flash freeze in liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in liquid nitrogen using ~30 cm tweezers, let them float briefly, then store immediately in an ultra‑low temperature (ULT) freezer.

steps.title: PBS wash before downstream use
steps.instruction: Remove supernatant, add 1–2 ml PBS, transfer worms to a 1.5 ml or 2 ml LoBind tube (fill only half), then spin 1 min at 10 000 rcf (room temperature).

steps.title: Weigh worm samples (optional)
steps.instruction: Weigh empty tubes, then weigh again after adding worms; 70–80 µl typically yields ≥60 mg, keep ≤100 mg per tube.

steps.title: Sucrose float wash
steps.instruction: Add 5 ml cold 60 % (w/v) sucrose to the tube; repeat this wash if bacterial contamination remains.

steps.title: Prepare liquid nitrogen safety
steps.instruction: Wear appropriate PPE, fill a small dewar with liquid nitrogen, and keep it ready for flash‑freezing steps.
